properties.description:
The algorithms the structural detectors run on, in-tree rather than obtained across a required interface: `GraphBuilder`, Leiden community detection, Tarjan SCC, connected components, directed cycle detection, articulation points and bridges (DFS lowlink), and Brandes betweenness centrality.

Consumed by `cmp:structure` and `cmp:allocate` (`sys:coherence-loop`) and `cmp:flow` (`sys:vocabulary`) — three consumers across two subsystems, which is why the component sits in `sys:foundation`.

⭐ EXACT, NOT APPROXIMATE, and that is a real property rather than an implementation note: upstream chose it on the ground that consumer graphs are 10^2-10^3 nodes, so there are no streaming or sampled variants. A design large enough to need them would need a different answer, and this capability does not provide one.

🛑 WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER: pagerank, eigenvector and closeness centrality, clustering coefficient, link prediction, max-flow/min-cut, shortest path, topological sort, degree centrality. 1,613 lines left upstream because nothing in reflow2 asks those questions. `cut_structure` in particular does NOT need max-flow — articulation points come from a DFS lowlink walk — which is the one closure result worth stating, because the intuition that "cuts need flow" would have dragged 248 lines in.

⚖️ Carries `#![allow(dead_code)]` on eight unused items, kept so the files stay byte-comparable with upstream. Anthony's call, 2026-08-24: trim later if still unused, not on the day it arrived.

(Distinct from `chg:absorb-graph-algorithms`, which records the MOVE and its measurements; this records what reflow2 can now do. The ChangeEvent is history, this is capability.)
properties.name: reflow2 owns the graph theory it analyses designs with
